drivingQuestion: When does a needle lodged in the wall of the reticulum render the animal a tereifa?
outcomeNote: A lemma and the baraita it introduces; the baraita's text runs on past the end of this unit.

segments.he: הֶמְסֵס וּבֵית הַכּוֹסוֹת, תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַחַט שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת בְּעוֹבִי בֵּית הַכּוֹסוֹת מִצַּד אֶחָד – כְּשֵׁרָה, מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִים – טְרֵפָה. נִמְצָא עָלֶיהָ קוֹרֶט דָּם –
segments.en: § The mishna states: An animal is a tereifa if the «omasum or the reticulum» was perforated to the outside, i.e., to the abdominal cavity. With regard to this, «the Sages taught:» In the case of «a needle that is found in the thickness of the reticulum,» if it pierced the wall «from» only «one side,» the animal is «kosher.» If it pierced the wall «from both sides,» i.e., the needle completely pierced the wall of the stomach, it is «a tereifa.» But even if it protrudes from both sides, it is not always a tereifa, and it may be inspected further: If «a drop of» congealed «blood is found on top of» the needle,
